cards.text: Jesus is still teaching on the Mount of Olives (Matthew 24:3). He just told about ten virgins waiting for a bridegroom, and now He gives another picture. It's just like a man going on a journey, who calls his servants and entrusts them with his possessions.

cards.question: The man gives one servant five talents, another two and another one. What decides how much each servant gets?

answers.text: How long each one has served

cards.text: Then the master leaves on his journey, and the five-talent servant goes at once and puts the money to work. No snooze button. No "I'll start Monday." Just GO.

cards.question: The five-talent servant puts the money to work right away. What does he gain?
True or false: The servant with two talents also gains as much as he was given.

cards.text: Two servants, two piles doubled. Now the one-talent servant goes off on his own.

cards.question: What does the one-talent servant do with his master's money?

answers.text: Digs a hole and hides it
Gives it away to the poor

cards.text: Into the ground it goes. Friend, I spent YEARS buried in the back of a junk drawer, and I promise you NOTHING grows back there. Well. The dust grew.

cards.question: True or false: The master of the servants comes back soon, before much time has passed.

cards.text: After a long time, the master comes back and settles accounts. The five-talent servant steps up first: "Master, you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more."

cards.question: The master tells the five-talent servant he's been faithful with ___ things, so he'll be put in charge of ___ things.

cards.text: And then he says, "Enter into the joy of your master!" Friend, if anybody ever said that to me, I'd frame it and hang it over the ovens. Then I'd point at it. Every. Single. Morning.

cards.question: The two-talent servant comes in with two more talents. How does the master's reply to him compare with what he told the five-talent servant?

answers.text: It's word for word the same
It comes with a stern warning

cards.text: Finally, the one-talent servant steps up and says, "Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed." Opening your performance review by telling the boss what's wrong with HIM? Bold, friend. BOLD.

cards.question: The one-talent servant says he knew his master was a hard man. What does he say he was, because of that?

cards.text: So he hid the talent in the ground, and now he hands it back: "See, you have what belongs to you." That's like getting handed cookie dough to bake and bringing back the same lump with dirt on it, like "Good news, I didn't burn it!"

cards.question: True or false: The master is pleased that the one-talent servant kept his money safe in the ground.

cards.text: The master answers, "You wicked, lazy servant!" Then he points out that the servant knew he reaps where he has not sown.

cards.question: If the servant knew all that, what does the master say he should have done with the money?

cards.text: Then on his return, the master would have received it back with interest. And honestly, friend? WAY less digging.

cards.question: The master orders the one talent taken from the lazy servant. Who does he say gets it?

answers.text: The one who has ten talents
The one who has four talents

cards.question: True or false: The master says the one who does not have will get to keep what he has.
Last, the master orders the worthless servant thrown out. Where to?

cards.text: Out there, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. That's where we'll leave this one for now, friend, but Jesus isn't done teaching yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "Master, you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card says Jesus is speaking but never says to whom. In Matthew 24:3 it is His disciples, who came to Him privately on the Mount of Olives.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card states a Bible fact from outside the passage, that Jesus just told about ten virgins waiting for a bridegroom, with no reference. It needs Matthew 25:1-13.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four sentences: the telling plus 'No snooze button.' 'No "I'll start Monday."' 'Just GO.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'Two servants, two piles doubled,' only recaps what cards 4 and 5 just answered. The rest of the card is stripped down, with no Papa Dorin voice.
The card is bare narration with no Papa Dorin voice. It reads as a stripped-down transition.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing new from the passage. 'Into the ground it goes' repeats the answer to card 7, and the rest is a joke. The joke should ride on a card that carries the next piece of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four sentences: 'Into the ground it goes.' 'Friend, I spent YEARS…' 'Well.' 'The dust grew.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The master's opening words, 'Well done, good and faithful servant!' (Matthew 25:21, 23), are never told or asked anywhere. Card 12 jumps to 'And then he says, "Enter into the joy of your master!"', and card 13 asks whether a reply matches when the baker has never seen that line.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four or more sentences: the quote, 'Friend, if anybody ever said that to me…', 'Then I'd point at it.' and 'Every. Single. Morning.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card runs to four sentences: the quote from verse 24, 'Opening your performance review…?', 'Bold, friend.' and 'BOLD.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card runs to three sentences: the telling, 'And honestly, friend?' and 'WAY less digging.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first half of Matthew 25:29, 'For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance,' is never told or asked. Card 9 only tests the second half, so the baker misses the principle the master gives for his ruling.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
